summary: Tested the Sound & Audio feature on the backend and frontend (mobile 390x844). Backend: 15 of 15 pytest tests pass for PATCH /api/user/preferences (partial updates, merge with defaults, persistence visible in /api/auth/me, 422 for volume -1/101/1000 and for a non-bool value, 0 and 100 accepted, unknown fields ignored, null does not overwrite, 401 without auth). Frontend: the Settings section renders with default-off state (toggle off, 50%, slider/output/test disabled, mic off). The sound toggle, volume (keyboard and click) and mic toggle all persist after a page reload. Turning the mic on called getUserMedia 0 times. No AudioContext and no extra /api/ws socket exist until sound is enabled; after enabling, exactly one extra /api/ws socket opens. The device list shows 3 fake devices in Chromium, so the radio list renders instead of the unsupported text. The test sound creates an AudioContext with no JS errors. In the chat header, chat-mute-btn toggles soundEnabled in the DB, and the icon and aria-label change. Sending works with sound on (outgoing tone played) and off (no tones). An incoming message from match_b played the incoming tone once while on and nothing while muted. English translations are correct. MatchCelebration was NOT tested end to end: pp-like is blocked by the profile-completion gate for match_a (expected), and the change there is a one-line useEffect(playSound('match')), checked by code review only. No page errors seen.

integration_issues.flow: micEnabled preference vs existing voice recorder
integration_issues.issue: ChatRoomPage already has a working voice-message recorder (mic button in the composer, navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia at ChatRoomPage.jsx:244), but micEnabled is never read there. The 'Microphone for voice messages' toggle therefore has no effect; recording works even with micEnabled=false. The brief says voice messages are not built yet, which does not match the code. Decide whether micEnabled should gate or hide the recorder button.

action_items: Minor: connect micEnabled to the existing chat voice recorder (hide/disable the mic button or show a hint when micEnabled=false), or relabel the setting.

Minor: useSoundPrefs.update() calls setSoundPrefs optimistically but has no try/catch. If PATCH fails, the in-memory sound prefs are left out of sync with the UI and no error toast appears. Revert and show a toast on error.
Minor: switches only flip after PATCH and refresh() round-trip (no optimistic UI state), so there is a short lag on slow networks.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend PreferencesBody uses Pydantic Field(ge=0, le=100) and exclude_none with dotted $set: correct, no _id leak.
WSManager keeps a set of sockets per user, so SoundManager's second socket does not break ChatRoom realtime, and is_online is handled correctly on disconnect.
Incoming sound plays only from SoundManager (not duplicated in ChatRoom): verified, one tone per incoming message.
sound.js getCtx is lazy, so nothing loads before the first playSound with sound enabled (or a forced test): verified.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (MatchCelebration sound checked by code review only)

seed_data_creation: Sent 4 chat messages between match_a and match_b (TEST_sound_on msg, TEST_incoming reply, TEST_sound_off msg, TEST_incoming muted); match_a's coins went from 252 to 250. Temporarily set testuser1 language_pref=en and restored it to ru. Preferences for testuser1, match_a and match_b were reset to soundEnabled=false, soundVolume=50, micEnabled=false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Language comes from user.language_pref, which overrides localStorage lovreski_lang; set it with PUT /api/profile {language_pref} to test English. Chromium headless exposes fake audio output devices, so sound-device-0..2 radios render.
